```{r loading packages and data}
library(dplyr)
library(tidylog)
library(janitor)
library(broom)
library(lubridate)
library(cancensus)
options(cancensus.api_key = "CensusMapper_9cd8925d1dd9197227f4bfaf596e0797")
library(here)
library(readxl)
library(stringr)

first_collection<- read_excel("Anonymized_Data/full_first_collection.xlsx")
column_clean_names<- read.csv("first_collection_cols_clean.csv")
```
```{r data clean}

first_collection_clean<-clean_names(first_collection)

#Keeping only the people who submitted the questionnaire, and manageing exclusions


first_collection_clean<- first_collection_clean %>%
  dplyr::filter(status=="Submitted") %>%
  dplyr::filter(exclude=="F") #Caolumn made to manage the developmental delay exclusions critically based on parents descriptions, also added the tests to be excluded


#Now let's select only the columns of data that we need

columns_drop<- c(2,3,4,5,7,10,11,12,15,17,20,25,26,27,28,36,37,38,39,40, 41,42,43,50,56,57,58,59,60,61,62,63,64,65,66,67,68,69,70,71,72,73,74,75,76,77,78,79,80,81,82,83,84,85,86,87,88,89,90,91,92,93,94,95,97,98,100,104,105,106,107,115,116,118,122,123,130,132,133,135,139,140,147,149,150,152,156,157,164,167,166,169,173,174,186,188,190,191,197,199,200,201)



first_collection_clean<- first_collection_clean%>%
  dplyr::select(-all_of(columns_drop))


# write.csv(
#   first_collection_clean,
#   here("Anonymized_Data/first_collection_clean.csv"),
#   row.names = FALSE
# )


first_collection_clean <- first_collection_clean %>%
  rename(!!!setNames(column_clean_names$old_names,
                     column_clean_names$new_names))


#Now let's get dates into the correct format 
first_collection_clean $survey_date<- as.Date(first_collection_clean $survey_date)
first_collection_clean $child_dob <- as.Date(first_collection_clean$child_dob)

#Let's make an age variable, calculated from the date of the survey and the date of birth
first_collection_clean$child_age_years <- time_length(
  interval(first_collection_clean$child_dob, first_collection_clean$survey_date),
  unit = "years"
) |> floor()








```

```{r wrangling predictors}

#here we need to make sure we have basically the same columns as in the new data, and coded the same way, e.g. numeric scale.


#language sources

first_collection_w_predictors <- first_collection_clean %>%
  mutate(
    caregiver_sources_english =
      (c1_percent_english_to_child >= 25 & !is.na(c1_percent_english_to_child)) + #counting as 1 values where parents speak the language to the child more than 25% of the time and values other than NA
      (c2_percent_english_to_child >= 25 & !is.na(c2_percent_english_to_child)),

    caregiver_sources_french =
      (c1_percent_french_to_child >= 25 & !is.na(c1_percent_french_to_child)) +
      (c2_percent_french_to_child >= 25 & !is.na(c2_percent_french_to_child)),

    caregiver_sources_first_minority =
      (c1_percent_first_minority_to_child >= 25 & !is.na(c1_percent_first_minority_to_child)) +
      (c2_percent_first_minority_to_child >= 25 & !is.na(c2_percent_first_minority_to_child)),

    caregiver_sources_second_minority =
      (c1_percent_second_minority_to_child >= 25 & !is.na(c1_percent_second_minority_to_child)) +
      (c2_percent_second_minority_to_child >= 25 & !is.na(c2_percent_second_minority_to_child)),

    caregiver_sources_third_minority =
      (c1_percent_third_minority_to_child >= 25 & !is.na(c1_percent_third_minority_to_child)) +
      (c2_percent_third_minority_to_child >= 25 & !is.na(c2_percent_third_minority_to_child))
  )

#pass the book access onto a numeric categorie and using a math formula (new score=2(old score)−1) to convert the categories onto a 7-point scale to match the sacle we use in the newer data collection

first_collection_w_predictors <- first_collection_w_predictors %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(
        book_resources_english_bookstore,
        book_resources_english_library,
        book_resources_french_bookstore,
        book_resources_french_library,
        book_resources_first_minority_bookstore,
        book_resources_first_minority_library,
        book_resources_second_minority_bookstore,
        book_resources_second_minority_library,
        book_resources_third_minority_bookstore,
        book_resources_third_minority_library
      ),
      ~ case_when(
        .x == "Very difficult" ~ 1,
        .x == "Somewhat difficult" ~ 3,
        .x == "Somewhat easy" ~ 5,
        .x == "Very easy" ~ 7,
        .x == "I'm not sure" ~ NA_real_,
        TRUE ~ NA_real_
      ),
      .names = "{.col}" 
    )
  )



#combine libraries and bookstore access. stick with the highest number.#naming the column the same as in the newer data for ease

first_collection_w_predictors <- first_collection_w_predictors %>%
  mutate(
    book_resources_english = if_else(
      is.na(book_resources_english_bookstore) &
        is.na(book_resources_english_library),
      NA_real_,
      pmax(
        book_resources_english_bookstore,
        book_resources_english_library,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    ),

    book_resources_french = if_else(
      is.na(book_resources_french_bookstore) &
        is.na(book_resources_french_library),
      NA_real_,
      pmax(
        book_resources_french_bookstore,
        book_resources_french_library,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    ),

    book_resources_first_minority = if_else(
      is.na(book_resources_first_minority_bookstore) &
        is.na(book_resources_first_minority_library),
      NA_real_,
      pmax(
        book_resources_first_minority_bookstore,
        book_resources_first_minority_library,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    ),

    book_resources_second_minority = if_else(
      is.na(book_resources_second_minority_bookstore) &
        is.na(book_resources_second_minority_library),
      NA_real_,
      pmax(
        book_resources_second_minority_bookstore,
        book_resources_second_minority_library,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    ),

    book_resources_third_minority = if_else(
      is.na(book_resources_third_minority_bookstore) &
        is.na(book_resources_third_minority_library),
      NA_real_,
      pmax(
        book_resources_third_minority_bookstore,
        book_resources_third_minority_library,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    )
  )


#DECIDED Mathematically convert down the 7 point scale to 6 to match. Just use speaking\
#In this case the mathematical conversion is new=(old−1)×5/6


first_collection_w_predictors <- first_collection_w_predictors %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(
        caregiver_1_english_proficiency,
        caregiver_2_english_proficiency,
        caregiver_1_french_proficiency,
        caregiver_2_french_proficiency,
        caregiver_1_first_min_proficiency,
        caregiver_2_first_min_proficiency,
        caregiver_1_second_min_proficiency,
        caregiver_2_second_min_proficiency,
        caregiver_1_third_min_proficiency,
        caregiver_2_third_min_proficiency
      ),
      ~ case_when(
        .x %in% 1:3 ~ 2,
        .x %in% 4:7 ~ 3,
        TRUE ~ NA_real_
      ),
.names = "{.col}"
    )
  )
#the problem with this formula is that we get decimal numbers, perhaps for the best to leave them decimal but could also convert to integers by rounding up or down


first_collection_w_predictors <- first_collection_w_predictors %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(
        child_english_active_use_category,
        child_french_active_use_category,
        child_first_min_active_use_category,
        child_second_min_active_use_category,
        child_third_min_active_use_category
      ),
      ~ recode(
        .x,
        "My child does not understand or speak this language" = 0,
        "My child understands this language, but rarely speaks in it" = 1,
        "My child speaks this language mainly when someone addresses them in that language" = 2,
        "My child speaks this language spontaneously" = 3
      )
    )
  )


first_collection_w_predictors <- first_collection_w_predictors %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(
        child_english_mixing,
        child_french_mixing,
        child_first_min_mixing,
        child_second_min_mixing,
        child_third_min_mixing
      ),
      ~ (.x - 1) * (5 / 6),
      .names = "{.col}"
    )
  )



```



```{r matchig columns to newer data}

#first drop the columns that are not in the new data

first_collection_w_predictors <- first_collection_w_predictors %>%
  select(-c("survey_date", "child_dob","attends_school","school_or_daycare","school_language","school_language_2","daycare_language","daycarte_language_2","has_siblings", "book_resources_english_library","book_resources_english_bookstore","caregiver_1_english_proficiency_comprehension",   
"caregiver_2_english_proficiency_comprehension","book_resources_french_library","book_resources_french_bookstore", "book_resources_first_minority_library","book_resources_first_minority_bookstore","caregiver_1_first_min_proficiency_comprehension", "caregiver_2_first_min_proficiency_comprehension","book_resources_second_minority_library","book_resources_second_minority_bookstore",         "caregiver_1_second_min_proficiency_comprehension","caregiver_2_second_min_proficiency_comprehension","book_resources_third_minority_library",           "book_resources_third_minority_bookstore","caregiver_1_third_min_proficiency_comprehension","caregiver_2_third_min_proficiency_comprehension",            "caregiver_1_french_proficiency_comprehension","caregiver_2_french_proficiency_comprehension","book_resources_first_minority_library", "multilingual_childrearing_reason","multilingual_chilrearing_concerns","exclude" ))



#save to call in the census analyses markdown

write.csv(
  first_collection_w_predictors,
  here("Anonymized_data/first_collection_w_predictors.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

```
